newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on late demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on late demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 140 basis points at 24.10 percent on Thursday due to late demand for paper, traders said.
"Rates reached attractive levels, so there was heavy dealing at the close," a trader said.
Traders added that rates had been under upside pressure for most of the day on speculation ahead of Banco de Mexico's daily participation in the market, which has seen changes this week.
The central bank drained 9.068 billion pesos through a combination of selling government paper and repurchase agrements.
Some dealers said Banco de Mexico drained a hefty amount of liquidity due to primary rates increasing little despite heavy demand at Tuesday night's auction.

"Primary rates are not high enough to keep foreign investment here, simply because they did not increase enough, so Banco de Mexico offers more (secondary) paper to jack up rates a little more," a money market analyst said.
In today's participation, Banco de Mexico effectively capped overnight rates at 25.73 percent, after which demand brought trading levels down and bolstered the peso.
Benchmark 48-hour peso rates ended 1.05 centavos firmer at 7.8750/7.8775 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper declined 100 basis points to close at 25.50 percent.
June Cetes futures contracts meanwhile closed up 40 centavos at 77.80 pesos on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Liquidity of 4.914 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
